# Ellen West

[Episcopalians](../codex/factions.md#episcopalians)

## Overview

- **Status:** alive  <sub>[v5 CHAPTER XXI. THE IMPOSSIBLE WORD P7](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0007)</sub>
- **Family:** [Leslie Moore](../character/leslie-moore.md) (relative), [Rosemary West](../character/rosemary-west.md) (sibling)

## Appearance

Ellen West is a dark, massive woman with black hair and thick, black eyebrows. She has a deep voice and clear, slaty blue eyes that resemble the gulf water in a north wind.

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER IV. THE MANSE CHILDREN P54](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0054), [v5 CHAPTER XIII. THE HOUSE ON THE HILL P25](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0025), [v5 CHAPTER XXXIV. UNA VISITS THE HILL P42](../source/v05-c34.md#nw-v05-c34-p0042)_

## Personality

Despite possessing a stern and forbidding initial appearance, Ellen is in reality a jolly individual with a hearty, gurgling laugh and a deep, mellow voice. She exhibits a sharp, pungent conversational style and possesses a distinctly stubborn nature.

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER XIII. THE HOUSE ON THE HILL P25](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0025), [v5 CHAPTER XIV. MRS. ALEC DAVIS MAKES A CALL P39](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0039), [v5 CHAPTER XXXII. TWO STUBBORN PEOPLE P47](../source/v05-c32.md#nw-v05-c32-p0047)_

## Traits

- jolly, with a hearty, gurgling laugh  <sub>[v5 CHAPTER XIII. THE HOUSE ON THE HILL P25](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0025)</sub>

## History

Ellen West resided at her home with her sister, [Rosemary](../character/rosemary-west.md), where she engaged [John Meredith](../character/john-meredith.md) in discussions regarding European politics and [German](../codex/factions.md#german) militarism during his visits. Holding [Rosemary](../character/rosemary-west.md) to a solemn vow they had made over their mother's Bible ten years prior never to marry, Ellen strictly warned her sister against romantic involvement with the widowed minister. When John proposed to [Rosemary](../character/rosemary-west.md), Ellen adamantly refused to release her sister from the promise despite Rosemary's pleas, leading [Rosemary](../character/rosemary-west.md) to send him a rejection. Later, after [Norman Douglas](../character/norman-douglas.md) asked [Rosemary](../character/rosemary-west.md) to release Ellen from her vow so they could marry, [Rosemary](../character/rosemary-west.md) freed Ellen from her promise. However, Ellen declared she would still not marry Norman if it meant leaving [Rosemary](../character/rosemary-west.md) to live alone on the hill.

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER IV. THE MANSE CHILDREN P1](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0001), [v5 CHAPTER IV. THE MANSE CHILDREN P6](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0006), [v5 CHAPTER IV. THE MANSE CHILDREN P9](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0009), [v5 CHAPTER IV. THE MANSE CHILDREN P11](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0011), [v5 CHAPTER IV. THE MANSE CHILDREN P12](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0012), [v5 CHAPTER IV. THE MANSE CHILDREN P13](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0013), +227 more_

## Quotes

> "When you howl you’re hit, I’ve always heard, George. But she promised, Saint—she promised, and we Wests always keep our word. So it won’t matter if he does want to philander, George. She promised. I won’t worry."
>
> — Ellen West — [v5 CHAPTER XIII. THE HOUSE ON THE HILL P40](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0040)

> "It is not nonsense. It is my firm decision. It would be absurd for you to think of living here by yourself—a mile from any other house. If you won’t come with me I’ll stay with you. Now, we won’t argue the matter, so don’t try."
>
> — Ellen West — [v5 CHAPTER XXXII. TWO STUBBORN PEOPLE P43](../source/v05-c32.md#nw-v05-c32-p0043)

> "I will not do it. A promise is a promise in my eyes. I will not do it. Break your promise—be forsworn if you will—but it shall not be with any assent of mine."
>
> — Ellen West — [v5 CHAPTER XXII. ST. GEORGE KNOWS ALL ABOUT IT P28](../source/v05-c22.md#nw-v05-c22-p0028)

> “I think it is just as well to be interested in things as long as you live,” she had said. “If you’re not, it doesn’t seem to me that there’s much difference between the quick and the dead.”
>
> — Ellen West — [v5 CHAPTER XXI. THE IMPOSSIBLE WORD P9](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0009)

> “I won’t have you always,” Ellen had said, breaking her silence with harsh intensity. “You will marry and leave me. I shall be left all alone. I cannot bear the thought—I cannot. I would rather die.”
>
> — Ellen West — [v5 CHAPTER XXI. THE IMPOSSIBLE WORD P20](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0020)

## Relationships

### [John Meredith](../character/john-meredith.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/ellen-west--john-meredith.md)

Ellen and [John Meredith](../character/john-meredith.md) are close friends who enjoy conversing about world affairs, European politics, and [German](../codex/factions.md#german) militarism. Despite their pleasant intellectual discussions, tension arises because Ellen suspects John has romantic intentions toward her sister, [Rosemary](../character/rosemary-west.md). Ellen actively warns [Rosemary](../character/rosemary-west.md) against courting the widowed minister, viewing his presence as a threat to a past promise.

- Friend of — close friends who enjoy discussing politics and world events  <sub>[v5 CHAPTER XXI. THE IMPOSSIBLE WORD P8](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0008)</sub>

### [Norman Douglas](../character/norman-douglas.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/ellen-west--norman-douglas.md)

Ellen is betrothed to [Norman Douglas](../character/norman-douglas.md), with whom she engages in friendly debates. However, their future together becomes uncertain due to a tangled web of past promises. Even after Norman confronts [Rosemary](../character/rosemary-west.md) to free Ellen from a childhood vow, Ellen refuses to marry him if it means leaving her sister to live alone on the hill.

- Romantically involved with — betrothed  <sub>[v5 CHAPTER XV. MORE GOSSIP P31](../source/v05-c15.md#nw-v05-c15-p0031), [v5 CHAPTER XXI. THE IMPOSSIBLE WORD P15](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0015), [v5 CHAPTER XXII. ST. GEORGE KNOWS ALL ABOUT IT P38](../source/v05-c22.md#nw-v05-c22-p0038), +3 more</sub>

### [Rosemary West](../character/rosemary-west.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/ellen-west--rosemary-west.md)

Ellen and [Rosemary](../character/rosemary-west.md) are sisters who share a deep bond bound by a solemn vow made ten years prior over their mother's Bible to never marry. When [John Meredith](../character/john-meredith.md) shows romantic interest in [Rosemary](../character/rosemary-west.md), Ellen strictly enforces this promise and refuses to release her, forcing [Rosemary](../character/rosemary-west.md) to send him a cold rejection. Although [Rosemary](../character/rosemary-west.md) eventually releases Ellen from the vow so she can marry [Norman Douglas](../character/norman-douglas.md), Ellen remains reluctant to leave her sister living by herself.

- Sibling of — sister  <sub>[v5 CHAPTER II. SHEER GOSSIP P66](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0066), [v5 CHAPTER IV. THE MANSE CHILDREN P50](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0050), [v5 CHAPTER XIII. THE HOUSE ON THE HILL P25](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0025), +9 more</sub>
